Responsive UX · Wireframe study

City of Phoenix

A low-fidelity reconstruction of a city website, examining hierarchy and the relationship between desktop and mobile layouts.

Explore the designs ↓
My role
Interface analysis & wireframe recreation
Tools
Figma
Deliverable
Desktop and mobile page wireframes

THE PROJECT

Overview

A city website serves many needs at once: residents looking for services, businesses finding resources, and visitors exploring the city. This study recreates that breadth as long-form desktop and mobile wireframes.

01 / DESIGN PROCESS

Map a layered information hierarchy

The desktop study combines audience navigation, service shortcuts, seasonal heat-relief information, news, and government resources. Actions such as paying, reporting an issue, finding trash information, and locating a park sit within a much larger page structure.

02 / DESIGN PROCESS

Translate the hierarchy to a narrow screen

The 390 px mobile wireframe studies how the same content can stack vertically. Comparing it with the 1440 px desktop layout makes the changes in grouping, density, and reading order visible. Scroll through either image or open it at full size to inspect the entire page.

REFLECTION

What this work shows

This study demonstrates responsive wireframing and the analysis of a large information hierarchy. It is a recreation exercise, rather than a commissioned redesign or a measured improvement to the city’s website.

Independent academic study. Original file: city of phoenix low fi wireframe recreation.fig.
